content:
Bloomberg reported that Apple may release a new Mac mini "as early as the next few days," potentially ahead of the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra launch event expected next month. Details below.

Likely the final product launch of Tim Cook's tenure

According to Mark Gurman, Apple is "preparing to release its first update to the Mac mini desktop in nearly two years," with surging demand partly driven by users wanting to run AI applications and models locally.

Original report:

Gurman added that Apple "has tested versions with two generations of processors, the M5 and M6," whereas the upcoming iMac refresh is reportedly set to use the M6 chip.

Weeks before tonight's report, Apple reiterated that it would begin production of the Mac mini later this year at its Houston facility, where Tim Cook toured with Trump administration officials.

The same site houses Apple's brand-new advanced manufacturing center, which has already been used to produce and ship the company's AI servers. Apple said earlier this month that it had invested hundreds of millions of dollars into the facility in less than nine months.

It remains unclear whether the new Mac mini expected in the next few days is the same model Apple plans to begin producing in Houston later this year, although the possibility is clearly high.

Gurman also reiterated several plans for Apple's Mac lineup in the coming months in his report:

More Mac computers are also on the way, but on a longer timeline. These include an iMac with new color options and an updated entry-level MacBook Pro. These products will use the upcoming M6 chip. And the most anticipated new Mac in the pipeline will be Apple's first touchscreen computer. The company will add this feature to a new generation of MacBook Pro models, offering 14-inch and 16-inch options, with a redesigned body and OLED displays.

Looking further ahead, Gurman reiterated earlier reports that Apple expects to release new MacBook Air and MacBook Neo models next year, along with a second-generation touchscreen MacBook Pro powered by the M7 chip.
